shorts.title: Biden Judge Tosses Brennan's Lawsuit Against Trump #Shorts
shorts.hook: A Biden Judge Just Ruled Against Brennan
shorts.narration: [serious] Folks, John Brennan, Obama's CIA chief, sued President Trump. And a Biden-appointed judge just tossed it. [beat] Judge Jia Cobb ruled Brennan's fears about destroyed evidence were, quote, "speculative." [sarcastic] Friends, he sued to stop the government from deleting texts he says he might need for an indictment that hasn't happened. [beat] That's not a lawsuit, that's a weather forecast. Brennan has not been charged, and his lawyers call the investigations baseless. Fair enough. [amused] But when your own side's judge says there's no standing, you've got a problem. Proverbs eighteen seventeen, King James: "He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him." [beat] Sue first, ask questions later, folks. So Democrats, tell me in the comments: if the case is so baseless, why sue before anyone charged him? Subscribe, Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: Judge Jia Cobb, a Biden appointee, dismissed former CIA Director John Brennan's lawsuit against President Trump and administration officials; she called his concerns about destruction of evidence "speculative" and found he lacked standing.
Brennan has been identified as a target in federal investigations but has not been charged; his lawyers called the investigations "baseless."
The lawsuit, filed July 1, 2026, argued key evidence such as texts and Signal messages could disappear before he could challenge an indictment.

slides.text: Director Brennan will continue to vigorously defend himself against these baseless investigations.

shorts.title: Flanagan On Minnesota Fraud: "The Buck Stops With Him" #Shorts
shorts.narration: [serious] Folks, Minnesota Senate debate. Republican Michele Tafoya asked Democrat Peggy Flanagan about the state's fraud scandal, investigators say up to nine billion dollars. [beat] Flanagan has been lieutenant governor since twenty nineteen. Her answer? Quote, "The governor has been very clear that the buck stops with him." [sarcastic] Friends, the buck stops with Walz. The lieutenant governor was just in the room. [beat] Tafoya's reply: "Peggy, Donald Trump isn't on the ballot. You and I are on the ballot." [amused] Ouch. Genesis three twelve, King James: "The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat." [beat] Blame-shifting, the oldest move in the Book. Democrats, tell me in the comments: eight years in the number two job, and nothing to own? Subscribe, Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: In an October 16, 2026 debate, Republican Michele Tafoya pressed Democrat Peggy Flanagan on Minnesota fraud; investigators have uncovered schemes accused of defrauding the state of up to $9 billion.
Flanagan said: "The governor has been very clear that the buck stops with him." and "He was the one who had oversight here."
Tafoya said: "Peggy, Donald Trump isn't on the ballot. You and I are on the ballot."
Flanagan has been lieutenant governor since 2019.

shorts.title: Trump On His New Press Secretary: "I Think You Should Reconsider" #Shorts
shorts.hook: Trump To His Press Secretary: Reconsider
shorts.narration: [serious] Folks, the White House press secretary job just got a new world record. Katie Zacharia was named on October ninth. [beat] Her first briefing, October thirteenth, ran fourteen minutes, three reporters. By Friday, Trump said, quote, "You don't have to do this if you don't want to. I think you should reconsider." [deadpan] Asked if he fired her, he said, "No no. I want her to have a good life." [beat] A senior official says she's "transitioning out." [sarcastic] Friends, that's the warmest firing in Washington history, and it still wasn't a firing. Ecclesiastes three one, King James: "To every thing there is a season." [beat] Hers was about seven days. Now tell me in the comments: who lasts longer, the next press secretary or the next Democratic talking point? Subscribe, Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: Katie Zacharia was named White House press secretary on October 9, 2026; her first briefing on October 13 lasted 14 minutes with questions from three journalists.
On Friday, October 16, Trump said: "You don't have to do this if you don't want to… I think you should reconsider."
Asked whether he fired her, Trump said: "No no. I want her to have a good life."
A senior White House official said she was "transitioning out"; Fox reported she was leaving after about seven days.
